result.summary:
Exclusion list for a new perf search, built from shared memory, git (all refs, fetched; main a44000e0), the four exp notes files, the perf doc sections 71.8 / 73 / 74, the roadmap Tier 5, the Phase 5 plan branch and archy's state file. Read-only; no cargo was run.

**s123 (wf_443f7b55-fcb, base c612dc7f): 21 candidates.** 7 survived and 14 were refuted (memory 13db18e4: "14 refuted (small gains/false premises)").
- Recovered by name: all 7 survivors and 3 of the 14 refuted.
- Survivors: 4 implemented (origin/exp/s123-*) and 3 dropped or folded (phase2-sharded-prepare, exec-prep-stage, exec-fused-keys).
- Refuted: consensus-reuse-action-hashes, next-leader-parent-path-slim, liq-scan-parallel-prevalue.
- The ranks in the notes are 1 cancel-all, 2 propose-defer, 3 exec-keys, 4 defer-book-blobs.
- Only one lens memory exists: b6d2198b, the exec/matching lens on main 46428bfa, with 4 candidates: cancel-all, PARALLEL_ENGINE, prep stage, liq scan.
- The four notes files list risks and not-done follow-ups, but no rejected candidates.
- None of the 4 branches is bench-ready. archy's state lists all 4 as PAUSED until 18c says tests pass.

**Notable facts:**
- (a) Conflict on exp/s123-parallel-cancel-all-book-pass at 73c99111. The commit message says "compile fixes in progress (not yet building or tested)". The notes file in the same commit has a "Build and test results" section: 36/36 targeted, 1784/1784 rdeps(torus-bridge) flag off and flag on, no new clippy warnings. 18c needs to confirm which is true.
- (b) propose-defer needs 2 consensus-timing fixes before it is built.
- (c) Item 7 step 1 C6 (863d2676) removes the EVM getOrderBook precompile (0x0800). That removes defer-book-blobs' main EVM risk once item 7 lands.
- (d) The sort-key half of exec-action-keys and cancel-all both edit native_executor.rs. Cancel-all must coordinate with Phase 5 step 3. propose-defer shares hotstuff_rs implementation.rs and torus-consensus app.rs with item 7.

**Other 18c work:**
- 71.8 option A (own RocksDB for the HotStuff and DA stores) is done and merged in a44000e0.
- Checkpoint batch slicing is the next item (sec 74.6: warranted, confidence medium). Not started per memory.
- Item 7 step 1 (EVM lanes) is being built: C1-C6 committed on 18c's local feat/item7-step1-evm-lanes, not pushed.
- Item 7 step 2 is designed. Item 6 Phase 5 is planned and decided but not started; it runs after item 7 steps 1-2.
- Roadmap Tier 5 (T5.1 block cadence, T5.2 p99 floor) comes after item 7 and Phase 5. Its measurement-only first steps can run on archy any time.

**archy's queue (all paused until the user says go):**
- TORUS_PARALLEL_ENGINE unset vs =8 A/B at 300m.
- The 4 exp branch A/Bs, once 18c says they pass.
- The slicing A/B, when 18c sends the branch.
- Set kernel.perf_event_paranoid=1 before the next perf campaign.

**Kinds beyond the six requested:**
- 'done' for merged work.
- 'prior-refuted' for older measured no-gain work cited by the s123 checks or by 18c's s111 shelved-gain sweep (memory cb3604fd). A new search would most likely re-propose these.
- 'prior-shelved' for one parked small item.

Memory saved: a short note on the recovery limits, tagged project:torus-hyperbft and experiment-s123.

items.name: parallel-cancel-all-book-pass
items.subsystem: torus-bridge native_executor.rs (exec_cancel_all_run, cancel_all_group, cancel_all_groups_parallel), market_workers.rs (run_contained now pub(crate) generic), cancel_batch_exec_tests.rs
items.change:
TORUS_PARALLEL_CANCEL_ALL=N (default off, cap 64) plus TORUS_PARALLEL_CANCEL_ALL_MIN_VISITS (default 64).
- What: the batched cancel-all book pass runs on exec_pool::run_jobs, one job group per market, chunked by MarketWorkerPool::chunk_indices (weight = members + 4).
- Book borrows: disjoint &mut books from one iter_mut pass.
- Margin: summed per market inside the job, in the same order, so no sum is reassociated.
- Panic: a worker panic latches fatal_error, the phase-1 caller returns before the cloid pre-pass and Phase 2, and the poisoned books are removed.
- Scope: the resident (P2-1) path only. Not changed: the non-resident path, single cancel_all, by-id cancels, liquidation cancels, torus-core, exec_pool.rs.
items.outcome:
Branch origin/exp/s123-parallel-cancel-all-book-pass at 73c99111: d2a7562c plus a WIP commit, on c612dc7f.
- Conflict: the commit message says not yet building. The notes in the same commit report a passing build (36/36 targeted, 1784/1784 rdeps flag off and on) plus a mutation check. Not bench-ready until 18c confirms.
- Owner paused the build/test so item 7 can finish. To resume: one background builder, CARGO_TARGET_DIR ~/.cargo-target-exp.
- Expected (inferred): phase1_actions ~26 to 8-12 ms per native block at N=8, block_ms -6 to -9%, matched/s +1.8 to 2.7% at 300m, about 0 at 10m. Bench-shape specific: every bench cancel is CancelAllOrders{None}.
- Gate before the A/B: re-profile phase 1 on head (the 27-of-30 ms per-book split is from 707f132f).
- A/B: 300m, ABBA n=4, unset vs =8.
- Must coordinate with item 6 Phase 5 step 3 (book dirty marks).

items.name: propose-defer-on-exec-queue
items.subsystem: hotstuff_rs app.rs (App::proposal_backpressure), hotstuff/implementation.rs (app_defers_proposal, APP_BACKPRESSURE_ESCAPE), proposal_backpressure_test.rs; torus-consensus app.rs
items.change:
The leader defers a fresh proposal while its own exec queue is at a watermark.
- hotstuff_rs: new trait method App::proposal_backpressure(), default false. It is OR'd with the existing S470 yield (TORUS_PROPOSER_EXEC_WATERMARK on pending headers + deferred bodies) at the retry path and the fresh Generic/Decide path. 300 ms escape before the view deadline. TC re-propose, nudges and votes are not gated.
- torus-consensus: TorusApp returns !exec_failed && exec_queue_len >= TORUS_PROPOSE_EXEC_WATERMARK. deferred_exec is deliberately not counted.
- Control arm: TORUS_EXEC_QUEUE_DEPTH (1..=64) on the exec sync_channel (64 = EXEC_QUEUE_DEPTH, torus-mempool rate_limit.rs:363).
items.outcome:
Branch origin/exp/s123-propose-defer-on-exec-queue at 662e5fab. Code only: never compiled or run.
- Static review: promising, determinism-safe (timing only).
- Must fix before building (review-issues.json on 18c): (1) bound the deferral per view independently of the leader's local deadline, which can carry up to 2x max_view_time of surplus; (2) skip the deferral when highest_tc.view+1 == current view (timeout-cascade risk).
- Expected (inferred): exec lag 64-66 down to about W (W=16), commit-to-exec 14-16 s down to 4-5 s, shock-to-liquidation about W+3 heights, RSS -0.25 to -0.35 GB per node, matched/s about +-2%.
- Bench: 300m arms main / DEPTH=16 / WATERMARK=16.
- Do not pair with TORUS_EXEC_NONBLOCKING_DISPATCH.
- Overlaps item 7's files.
- Related prior work: s77 TORUS_EXEC_THROTTLE_WATERMARKS cost -25% matched/s; S470 proposer watermark already exists.

- Gate: flag on, VerifyMode not Serial, n >= 16.
- The live caller is app.rs:3370.
items.outcome:
Branch origin/exp/s123-exec-action-keys-parallel at 129ca92f. Code only, not built.
- Static review: promising, flag-off path identical.
- Review advice: run an in-process microbench (270 warm 268-order batches) first, and log trust-cache hits and misses (the 300m hit rate is undocumented).
- Expected (inferred): exec_verify 11.5 to 1.5-3 ms per native block, block_ms -4 to -5%, matched/s +1 to +1.5% at 300m, about 0 at 10m. May expose end_resident_wait by 0-2 ms.

items.name: defer-book-blobs-in-layer-merge
items.change:
TORUS_CKPT_DEFER_BOOKS=1 (default off) adds CF_NATIVE_ORDER_BOOKS to the deferred-slot table.
- Gated on Classic book rows (TORUS_BOOK_ROWS not 1/2/3) and resident books (TORUS_RESIDENT_BOOKS not 0).
- Effect: Classic book blobs (77% of state bytes) merge in the checkpoint layer's deferred part, so exec's block-start settle waits only for markets and sessions.
- split_deferred, merge_part and NativeStateOverlay::layer_for all read the same table. No app.rs or backend.rs edits.
items.outcome:
Branch origin/exp/s123-defer-book-blobs-in-layer-merge at 5296115f. Code only, not built.
- Static review: promising; flag-off identical; checkpoint batch byte-identical.
- Expected: checkpoint_settle_wait 8.8 to under 1.5 ms per native block in soak (3.1-4.4 to under 1 ms in SAT). block_ms -2.5 to -3.5% in soak; SAT within noise; matched/s likely a tie; commit p99 unchanged.
- Guards: torus_exec_checkpoint_deferred_read_waits_total must stay 0; watch engine ms per 1k fills (memcpy contention).
- Risks:
  - The EVM getOrderBook precompile waits for the whole deferred part. Item 7 step 1 C6 removes that precompile.
  - Resident-book rebuild (load_order_books) waits too.
  - Exporting the flag breaks two unit tests.
- Prior basis: memory 1e1cde98 (s114 p3 merge-wait) had kept books in Main only because of the non-resident mode.

items.name: consensus-reuse-action-hashes
items.subsystem: torus-consensus app.rs (PendingProposal::new :6994, select scan :7640-7644, cold streaming :1293-1310, dispatch rehash :8004-8011, mirror :6626-6632)
items.outcome:
keep=false. Keccak is 0.07-0.09 of the hotstuff-algo thread's 0.17-0.18 cores at 300m, so the saving is about 0.05 core per node (~1% CPU).
- 300m is exec-bound and 10m is wave-shaped (sec 70.5), so the premise that the chain is consensus-bound is wrong.
- s66 TORUS_DEFER_COMMIT_FEED gave no gain.
- Low-priority CPU hygiene only. Side finding: the select in-flight scan is redundant in compact mode because the in_flight_hashes ledger covers it.

items.name: next-leader-parent-path-slim
items.change: The same compact-hash reuse as consensus-reuse-action-hashes, plus a parallel bincode decode in NativeDaStore::get_batch_timed.
items.outcome:
keep=false.
- The hash half nearly duplicates consensus-reuse-action-hashes.
- DA decode is 12-16 ms mean, and only on the 33-48% of views where the body is late.
- s76 step 2 already cut late-view validate by 15-19 ms with no throughput gain. Consensus-thread cuts in s66, s67, s68 and s72 D were flat.
- A parallel decode needs a new pool: torus-state has no rayon, the exec pool is exclusive, and the global pool starved consensus in s352.
- Roadmap T5.1 says attribution first.

items.outcome:
REJECT.
- Gain: about 4-6 ms of 206-239 ms block_ms, i.e. +0.6 to +0.8% matched/s, below the n=4 CI of about +-1.3%.
- The 62% liq_view share comes from sec 37.4 on Phase 3 step 0 and was not re-profiled.
- Phase 5 steps 2 and 5 rewrite this path.
- The memo Mutex and overlay RwLock are taken about 4x per trader, and 3 nodes share one host.

items.name: checkpoint batch slicing (sec 74 next step)
items.subsystem: torus-state checkpoint flush / state-DB WriteBatch path (shared write queue); consensus on_committed_block commit-manifest put
items.change:
Write the ~200 MB checkpoint WriteBatch in slices, so queued state-DB writers get in between. The queued writers are the commit-manifest put in on_committed_block, persist_committed_block_durably and the other state writers.
- Before the run: add a bucketed timer around persist_commit_manifest and keep the consensus-thread timer buckets in the sampler.
- Narrower alternative, not chosen: move the commit manifest off the state-DB queue. It leaves 0.06-0.14 s/s of other writers and changes the crash ordering.
items.outcome:
Sec 74.6 verdict: warranted, confidence medium. After option A, B's remaining in-window wait (0.21 s/s) is all on the state DB; commit-manifest put is +25 ms per call in windows.
- No memory says the build has started. 18c is expected to send a branch.
- archy will A/B the slicing prototype against option A: 300m, 600 s, n=3 (n=4-5 to resolve ~200 ms), ABBA. Success: in-window block p99 within ~100 ms of out-of-window, and on_committed_block equal in and out of windows.
- perf needs perf_event_paranoid <= 1.

result.metrics:
CELL (tools/matched-bench/run-cell.sh, one 3-validator devnet on archy, devnet/wsl, RPC 8645-8647). The bench (bench-throughput consensus --econ) uses 5,000 senders (offset 60) and M markets drawn uniformly (MPS unset). Each place action carries a batch of 400 orders. Other flags: submit-batch 1, binary format, concurrency 256, rate-total 76,000 (saturating), cross 0.5, cancel 0.05, band 5.

The current standard shape adds:
- BLOCK_CAP=400 (400 actions, 12 MB body).
- MAX_IN_FLIGHT=4 per sender, so 20,000 actions in flight. A slot frees when the action is seen in a committed body.
- OPEN_ORDER_BUDGET=900: two 400-order places, then a cancel-all. About 38-39% of actions are cancel-alls.
- RETRY_BUSY=1.
- IN_FLIGHT_TAIL=commit at tail depth 1: the bench reads val2's torus_getBlockBody one body at a time. Depth 4 reads ahead.
- ORACLE_FEED=1 (30000, 2,000 ms, walk 0), CLOID_SHARE=0, Classic books, 15 s checkpoints (validator default), jemalloc compiled in.
- TORUS_ROCKSDB_STATS=2 in the latency campaigns.

Durations: 120 s for throughput gates, 600 s for latency and soak cells. A 60 s warm-up cell is excluded. Drain needs 10 s of unchanged counters.

DEFINITIONS (summary.json from summarize.py; analyst a-cells.py / j3.py):
- matched/s = headline.matched_s_avg: the delta of val0's torus_orders_matched_total (fills) over the bench window [t_bench0, t_bench1] (summarize.py:1307). Never computed bench-side. Use matched_s_first120 to compare cells of different length; there is also an incl-drain variant.
- native blk/s: val0's delta of torus_exec_engine_seconds_count divided by the load-window span (summarize.py ~309).
- exec busy = delta of exec_block_seconds_sum / span.
- exec block_ms: exec-thread wall per native block, including the cost of empty blocks (phase_by_node.block_ms; chain_ms is the serial chain). a-cells averages the 3 nodes. Always read it next to fills_per_native_block and engine_ms_per_1k_fills, because block size drifts at saturation.
- Phases are per-native-block timers:
  - engine = phase1_actions + margin + match + settle (pass_a, pass_b and cache_flush are nested inside settle) + post_engine_tail + engine_untimed.
  - residual_untimed = block_ms minus all exec-thread timers.
  - flush and end_resident are worker time (off_chain).
- block p99 (sections 61-74) = commit-interval p99: the gaps between consecutive 'on_commit_block fired height=' lines in val*.log.gz within the bench window, p99 per validator, then the mean of 3 (a-cells.py blocks()).
- In/out of window (j3.py): a window is any node's torus_flush_worker_checkpoint_seconds step, widened by the 1 s scrape; the first 20 s are skipped. 40-46% of seconds count as in-window.
  - Section 73 used the 1 Hz torus_commit_interval_seconds histogram instead (factor-2 buckets, max over nodes), which is an upper bound only.
  - headline commit_interval_ms_p50/p95 are interpolated within buckets.
- CPU-s/1M = node user+sys CPU from /proc/pid/stat (procstat.raw -> proc_cpu_by_node.whole_run) divided by whole-run fills in millions, mean of 3 nodes. When throughput differs, compare at equal fills (ANCOVA).
- RSS = VmRSS.
  - a-cells: cpu.csv (10 s samples), per-node mean and peak over the cell, mean of 3 nodes, GB = kB/1e6.
  - Sections 73-74: mem-samples.txt (5 s samples, bench window).
  - Soaks: mean of minutes 5-10.
  - The handoff rss_mean_GB uses a different window.
- Bytes written: device write_bytes per node from /proc/pid/io (io-ticks.txt, 1 Hz), in MB/s per validator. RocksDB WAL bytes per DB come from torus_rocksdb_* in sampler.csv; state DB and consensus DB are separate since a44000e0.
- Consensus timeouts = headline.consensus_timeouts, val0's delta of torus_consensus_timeout_total (summarize.py:1336).
- AGREE (agreement.jsonl) requires all of:
  - height spread <= 5;
  - equal block hash and header stateRoot at a block every node serves;
  - equal sha256 state digest (every market's book, open interest, and 50 sender balances; plus vault and escrows in liquidation cells);
  - equal counters;
  - zero panic / FAIL-STOP lines.
  - validity ACCEPT also needs liveness PASS (no 30 s commit freeze), a completed drain and clean dissemination.
- Other series used here:
  - torus_exec_queue_depth = committed minus executed heights. Bound 66 = 64 channel + 1 executing + 1 blocked send. Exact only with TORUS_EXEC_NONBLOCKING_DISPATCH unset.
  - sched_by_node (schedstat): on-CPU and runqueue-wait ms per committed block for torus-execution and hotstuff-algo.
  - consensus_by_node.load: view, proposal arrival, block build/select/mirror, insert/commit persist, on_committed_block, qc_to_advance.
  - Per-thread CPU: io-threads-{start,end}.txt, columns pid tid comm read_bytes write_bytes wchar utime stime, in ticks at 100/s. Written by /home/oz/bench-results-matched/ozarchy-p3s0r-tools/io-sampler.sh at bench start and bench end.

result.noise_rules:
REPLICATE NOISE (matched/s):
- 300m 120 s cells: CV 0.38-0.88% (67.3), up to 1.45% for one arm (68.1). A sd 924 = 0.41% (73.2).
- 300m 600 s cells: sd ~0.4% (74.1: A 225.1-226.5k, B 226.9-228.5k).
- 10m 120 s: CV 0.20-0.67%. 10m 300 s cells: residual SD 0.60% (70.1).

CONFIDENCE INTERVALS:
- The '±1.3%' reference holds: n = 4 paired ABBA t(3) gives about ±1.3% at 300m (67.3: +3.01 [+1.69, +4.33]) and about ±1.0% at 10m.
- n = 3 Welch with t = 4.303 (df 2): about ±2.3% for 120 s cells (73.2) and about ±0.85% for 600 s cells (74.1).
- Block-level metrics are much noisier than matched/s because block size drifts at saturation (44.7k-51.3k fills per block across same-arm cells, 68.2): native blk/s paired CI ±13.6 pp and block_ms ±11 pp (67.3).
- Block p99: per-cell sd ~72 ms (71.1). n = 3 leaves CIs of about ±210 ms; resolving a ~200 ms step needs n = 4-5 per arm (74.6).
- CPU-s/1M is tight: a 0.7% step resolved at n = 3 (74.1). Compare at equal fills (ANCOVA) when matched/s moves, because fixed costs spread over more fills.
- RSS: 120 s cells are still warming up (+0.9 to +1.3 GB/min). Judge RSS level on 600 s soaks, minutes 5-10.

CHECKING THE REFERENCE POINTS:
- '+3.0% matched/s per -10.2% block_ms' (67.4) is NOT an elasticity. The block_ms paired CI included 0 ([-21.4, +1.1]), and part of the drop is smaller blocks (+9.5% blk/s).
  - Use exec wall per 1k fills (block_ms / fills_per_native_block) and busy: matched/s = busy x fills per exec-second, which held within ~2% here.
  - Or use the plans' rule: +0.4-0.55% matched/s per ms saved per native block at 200-250 ms blocks (item6-phase2-impl.md:55); that is ~0.3%/ms at the 313 ms blocks of 600 s cells.
  - Closed-loop caveat (sections 54, 67): per-block savings can show up as more, smaller blocks with matched/s tied. Target per-fill cost for matched/s.
- '300m exec-bound' is confirmed: busy 0.98-0.997, queue 60 of 66.
- '10m wave-shaped' holds only at tail depth 1. At depth 4 the waves vanish and 10m is exec-bound too.

DECISION RULES:
- Every cell must be ACCEPT AGREE. DISAGREE rejects the candidate. Known non-fork artifacts:
  - the mark-only digest (5 mark fields only);
  - 10m 'block not served yet' ERR (harness fix a91ce47c).
- n = 1 is not a result (README). Gates use n = 4 ABBA 120 s. Latency campaigns use n = 3 ABBA 600 s (raise to 4-5 for p99).
- Phase gate template (Phase 4 section 1):
  - matched/s up with the paired-CI lower bound >= 0 at 300m;
  - native blk/s no regression;
  - no 10m regression in the same campaign;
  - CPU-s/1M no regression beyond noise.
  - Phase 5 adds block p99 no regression and crab overhead <= +15% per fill.
- Stop rules:
  - Phase 4 step 0: ~2% of exec-thread wall.
  - Phase 5 step 0: removable ms x ~0.4% must reach the gate.
  - Owner s119: keep a step only if it nets a gain after its upkeep (step 5 was dropped).
- THE 5% LINE: the Phase 3 sizing rule was '>= 5% node CPU-s/1M saving that clears the noise' (sections 41-42). At 4.90% it shelved Phase 3; the owner reversed that in s111 and replaced it with the matched/s + blocks/s gate. Treat 5% as historical, not a current rule.
- Gate 3 target: >= 1.4x vs 199bdc97 (met at 1.93x).

TRAPS:
- Compare cells of different length only on matched_s_first120. 600 s and 120 s cells differ in block size (~72k vs ~50k fills) and in save_books per fill.
- Histogram p99s (factor-2 buckets) are upper bounds; use the log-based a-cells / j3 method.
- perf only on val1 (val0 serves the bench RPC and the headline). perf costs ~1.3% (64.1).
  - paranoid 2 means only cycles:u works; context-switches:u records 0 samples (74.4).
  - perf build-id cache hardlink trap: run perf script with --symfs (63, 69.7).
- 10 s windows alias with the ~13.5 s 10m wave; use 60 s windows or whole waves. Fix and record the tail depth per market count.
- Quiet host: no cargo, rustc, rust-analyzer, perf, indexer or Codex during cells (a Codex review cost -14%, 65.3). Run cells as systemd units through detach.sh, one bench at a time, never build during a bench. Interleave arms (ABBA or rotated rounds): non-interleaved c0 cells drifted (63.2).
- Exec queue depth equals lag only with TORUS_EXEC_NONBLOCKING_DISPATCH unset.
- jemalloc decay settings cost throughput (M1 -7.1%, M0 -30.7%); keep the defaults (73.4).
result.host:
HARDWARE (archy / ozarchy):
- AMD Ryzen 9 5950X: 16 cores / 32 threads (SMT2), 2 CCDs x 32 MB L3 (64 MiB), one NUMA node.
- 62 GB RAM. One shared NVMe (btrfs data dirs).
- Kernel 7.2.5-3-omarchy-bore (BORE scheduler); THP always.
- vm.dirty_bytes 256 MiB / dirty_background_bytes 64 MiB (as found; no sudo).
- perf_event_paranoid 2: user-space perf only, no sched tracepoints.

TOPOLOGY:
- 3 validators (devnet/wsl; RPC 8645-8647, metrics 9161-9163), the bench-throughput client and the oracle feed share the host. Quorum is 3/3.
- val0: the bench submit RPC and the headline counters.
- val2: serves the bench commit tail (torus_getBlockBody); 4 hot rpc-worker threads, ~0.78 core, ~+10% node CPU.
- val1: the profiled node.

THREADS PER NODE (from io-threads):
- torus-execution: 1 serial exec thread (~0.83 core at 300m) plus 32 idle namesakes.
- torus-exec-pool: 32 (rayon; size = max(available_parallelism, TORUS_MATCH_WORKERS, TORUS_SETTLE_WORKERS), all default to 32).
- torus-gossip-verify 16 and torus-ingress-verify 16 (available_parallelism / 2).
- tokio-rt-worker 32.
- RPC runtime: 4 workers plus a blocking pool (~73-76 threads named rpc-worker).
- One each: hotstuff-algo, rocksdb:high, torus-flush-worker, torus-end-resident, torus-ckpt-drop. rocksdb:low: 3. Plus ckpt-merge, trade writer and DA recovery threads.
- Across 3 nodes that is ~96 exec-pool + 96 verify + 96 tokio threads on 32 hardware threads.

LOAD:
- 300m 600 s: nodes use 4.6-5.2 cores each (val2 highest), bench ~1.25 cores, ~16-17 of 32 CPUs busy. load1 average ~29 (max 46). Exec-thread runqueue wait 8.4 ms per native block (2.7%); hotstuff-algo 4.5 ms per committed block.
- 300m 120 s: nodes 3.4-4.1 cores each, bench 1.4; exec runqueue wait 6.5-7.1 ms per block.
- 10m: nodes 3.8-4.4 cores (depth 1) or 4.5-5.4 (depth 4); bench 1.5-1.7; load1 23-33.
- 300m CPU share by thread group (fleet, current main code): exec-pool 21.8%, gossip-verify 18.1%, exec thread 16.1%, ingress-verify 15.3%, tokio 8.3%, rpc-worker 7.2%, rocksdb:low 5.0%, hotstuff 3.6%, rocksdb:high 1.4%, flush 1.3%, end-resident 1.2%.

MEMORY AND DISK:
- RSS per node: 5.7-5.8 GB mean, 6.5-6.6 GB peak at 300m 600 s; 2.75 / 3.3 GB at 10m.
- Disk at 300m: ~85 MB/s device writes per node, ~255 MB/s for the host. Checkpoint windows reach 0.32-0.87 GB/s across the 3 nodes.

PIPELINE CONSTANTS:
- Exec channel: std sync_channel(64), blocking send from the consensus thread.
- View timeout base 1,200 ms (genesis timeout_base_ms).
- Checkpoints every 15 s, ~200 MB per node at 300m.
- Own consensus RocksDB since a44000e0 (cf_consensus_meta, cf_native_pending, cf_native_shards; 64 MiB cache, 256 MiB memtables); 0 stalls in every cell.

PINNING: CPU-set pinning per node was tested once, on an old build (s75, e12bdac): -5.7%, not adopted. Worker caps per node have not been varied on current builds.

result.summary:
Map of perf work already done on Torus-hyperBFT up to main a44000e0 (2026-10-15). Read-only; no files edited, no cargo run.

Sources and abbreviations:
- **R§N**: docs/perf/ozarchy-antispam-item6-pf1-2026-10-04.md section N, plus its Open list.
- **M200k**: matched-200k-campaign-2026-08-18.md. **BL**: block-latency-campaign-2026-08-20.md. **TC**: throughput-campaign-2026-09-18.md.
- **s64 / s65**: the explorer syntheses. **sNN doc**: docs/perf/sNN-*.md.
- **P1 / P2 row N**: review-log rows in docs/plans/item6-phase1-impl.md and item6-phase2-impl.md.
- **mem**: a memory id. **git**: a commit.
- Knob defaults were checked in the source.

Where main stands now (per the sibling bottleneck map, mem 2a94cf27, and section 74 arm B, which is the same code as main):
- **300 markets:** about 225-227k matched/s. It is exec-bound: exec busy 0.97-0.995, with about 61 heights waiting at the 64-block exec channel.
- **10 markets:** about 300k matched/s. At bench tail depth 1 the load comes in waves set by the bench's tail. At depth 4 it is exec-bound.

The biggest merged levers:
- Item 6 Phases 1-4: Gate 3 is 1.93x the pre-item-6 main.
- Phase 3 checkpoints every 15 s: CPU -9.7%, device writes -55%, matched/s +8.8%.
- Native trie maintenance off: +31% at 300 markets.
- Trade history off on validators: CPU -12%.
- P2-5 foldhash hasher: matched/s 1.036x (+3.6%).
- jemalloc: native blocks/s +15%.
- Cloid fixes: +5.6% when every order carries a cloid.
- HotStuff and DA stores in their own RocksDB: in-window DB write wait -91%.

Cutting consensus-thread work repeatedly left throughput flat. This covers the vote DB, the DA-rewrite skip, the deferred feeds, the collector local advance and reusing action hashes. Execution, not consensus, is the limit.

Items marked avoid=false, worth revisiting because the baseline changed:
- Slicing the checkpoint batch, a 60 s interval, or staggering checkpoints across validators.
- Deciding WAL compression again, as the owner asked, now that Phase 3 is merged.
- TORUS_PARALLEL_ENGINE at today's ~100k orders per block.
- Worker-pool caps: each of the 3 nodes defaults to 32 threads on one 32-thread host.
- The production hash-only push threshold and shard custody: the bench turns both off or changes them.
- WAL-off for the state write.
- Release-profile LTO, never tried.
- Bench tail depth 4, which is not on main.
- The 4 s123 experiments: coded on branches exp/s123-*, not built yet.
- Phase 5, which is planned.

candidates.title: Let epoch-boundary blocks use the pipelined fast path instead of a synchronous checkpoint-drain barrier
candidates.mechanism:
Bench and testnet genesis use epoch_length = 100, so every height divisible by 100 is an epoch boundary. The `pipelined` predicate (app.rs:3014-3019) sends every boundary block down the serial path. pipeline_barrier (app.rs:2377-2391) first calls checkpoint_drain, which closes the open checkpoint window into a forced checkpoint, then worker.wait_idle, so the exec thread blocks until W has written that checkpoint. At 300m even a 2-6 s window is about 54-170 MB, because the book blobs dominate. The boundary block then executes serially, including its own ~53 MB flush on the exec thread (exec_flush_seconds: 26 calls, 3.09 s, 119 ms each).

Proposed change: a node-local flag, default off, lets boundary blocks with no EVM tx and no slash take the existing fast path. The block's rows then go into the checkpoint layer. The height-%100 attest checkpoint is already `due` on the fast path (app.rs:2626-2631), so it is submitted asynchronously. The exec thread no longer waits for the drain write or does the serial flush.

Why the original reasons no longer force a barrier:
- F2 (the EVM account resync): W already gathers evm_addrs in Digest jobs and resyncs them after the checkpoint lands (exec_pipeline.rs:818, 872).
- F8 (a consensus-thread staking writer): removed by bug (b) (732c78ed). Consensus now only reads the plan, after the durable applied height reaches H-L (app.rs:6541-6551).

Only the timing of the plan's durability changes. It becomes durable when the async checkpoint lands, within about 1-2 s. Consensus needs it about 34 or more blocks later, because the exec queue holds at most 66 heights and L = 100.

candidates.evidence:
Measured on current-main code: the hsdb arm B cells, crates/ byte-identical to a44000e0. Method: /tmp/liqlens/epoch2.py over val*.log.gz. The barrier gap is the time from the previous block's 'block done' to the boundary block's 'executing finalized block'. Section 64.3's 538-vs-358 ms comparison does not include this gap.

300m, 600 s cells (/home/oz/bench-results-matched/ozarchy-hsdb-300m-r{1,2,3}-B, 9 node-cells):
- Every height%100 block in the bench window ran pipelined=false.
- Barrier gap: 499-526 ms mean per node.
- Serial block: 364-479 ms, against a pipelined mean of 344-349 ms.
- Excess per epoch: 534-639 ms. With 18-19 epochs per cell, that is 1.60-1.98% of exec time lost.
- The boundary block was committed 5-22 s before exec finished B-1, so it was already queued and the gap is entirely exec-side.

Checkpoint data (metrics-after-val1 and ckpt-samples.txt):
- W wrote 59 checkpoints in 46.2 s; 14 of them fall in the 0.256-0.512 s bucket. These are the epoch drains, 54-170 MB each, 2-8 s after an interval checkpoint.
- exec_flush_seconds: 26 serial flushes, 119 ms mean.

Other cells:
- 300m, 120 s (ozarchy-p4j4h-300m-r{1,2,3}-A on bdd59888; ozarchy-p4gate-300m-*): 1.5-2.6% of exec time, with only 4-6 epochs per cell.
- 10m, depth 4 (ozarchy-p4tail10-10m-r1-{a4,b4}): 1.3-1.5%.
- 10m, depth 1: the gap is only 80-90 ms and exec is not the limit (busy 0.77).

At 300m exec busy is 0.995 and the exec queue holds 60 of 66, so lost exec time is lost fills.

What this does not affect:
- Consensus timeouts: only 2-4 of 13-18 per cell fall near a stall, against 18% time coverage.
- Block p99: 0-57 ms per node; not resolvable.
candidates.est_gain:
Recoverable time per epoch is about 0.5 s: W's drain write (~0.38 s) plus the serial flush (~0.12 s). The take_layer/merge upkeep stays, because it runs on the fast path too.
- 300m, 600 s: matched/s +1.3 to +1.8%, native blk/s about the same. Exec block_ms -4.5 to -5.5 ms per native block (-1.5 to -1.8%), almost all of it out of residual_untimed.
- 300m, 120 s gate cells: +1.5 to +2.5%.
- 10m depth 4: +1.0 to +1.3%.
- 10m depth 1: about 0.
- Device writes: about -0.9 GB per node per 600 s, because the ~53 MB serial flush is coalesced into the checkpoint.
- CPU-s/1M: 0 to -0.3%.

The change also removes a hidden source of variance in 120 s cells: the 4-6 barriers per cell are each worth about 0.4-0.5% of the cell.
candidates.determinism: Byte-identical state. The flag only routes no-EVM, no-slash boundary blocks to the existing fast path, which more than 99% of blocks already use and which is differential-tested against the serial path. Every boundary write goes through ctx.staking on the block overlay into the same FrozenPending: rewards, inflation credits, the rotation plan, the epoch_vset rows and validator statuses. Dirty EVM accounts are resynced on W after the write, as for any pipelined block. Crash replay is always serial from the durable marker. The flag changes only when the plan and marker become durable, which affects the liveness-only `applied >= H-L` check: consensus refuses and retries, it never reads different content. Mixed fleets agree.
candidates.flag: TORUS_EPOCH_FAST_PATH=1 (node-local, default off). Off is exactly main's predicate: `!is_epoch_boundary` stays in `pipelined`.
candidates.impl_size: S: about 10 lines (a OnceLock env parse plus one predicate term), optionally an exec_barrier_seconds timer around pipeline_barrier so the stall shows in summary.json, plus about 3 tests.
candidates.test_plan:
Write the tests first (torus-consensus app.rs tests):
1. epoch_boundary_fast_path_identical_to_serial:
   - epoch_length 4 and 100 (205 blocks), flush worker attached.
   - Checkpoint policies: per-block (None), every 5 blocks, never (attest-only).
   - Random native blocks plus a delegation/stake change at boundary-1 and a key rotation.
   - Compare flag off against flag on: dump_all_cfs after each block (epoch_vset rows, CF_STAKING_*, CF_ACCOUNTS and CF_HASHED_ACCOUNTS after wait_idle for F2), the running hash per height, and the action status.
   - Assert boundary blocks did not hit pipeline_barrier when the flag is on. RED until the flag exists.
2. epoch_boundary_fast_path_plan_ready_for_next_boundary: epoch_validator_set_updates(H+L) returns Err(EpochPlanNotReady) while W is gated before the %100 checkpoint, and after wait_idle it equals flag-off.
3. Crash: gate W before the boundary checkpoint, drop, restart; the serial replay matches (reuse ckpt_crash_replay_on).

Then run `cargo nextest run -p torus-consensus` and `-E 'rdeps(torus-state)'`.

Bench on archy:
- 300m, 600 s, ABBA, n=3-4, flag unset vs =1. Also 10m depth 1, n=4, to show no regression.
- Mechanism checks: pipelined=false count goes to 0; the gap at h%100 drops from ~500 ms to ~0; exec_flush_seconds_count goes to ~0; torus_exec_checkpoints_total is unchanged; the 'validator-set plan not ready' warn count stays 0.
- Report matched/s, native blk/s, block_ms and residual_untimed, CPU-s/1M, device writes, consensus timeouts and block p99. Every cell must be ACCEPT AGREE.
candidates.novelty_check:
Not proposed before, as far as I could find:
- Memory: searches on 'epoch boundary barrier / unpipelined / checkpoint drain' and 'pipeline_barrier epoch F2 F8' found no prior proposal.
- The AVOID and revisit lists have no epoch item.
- Git (all refs) has no epoch knob or branch.
- Section 64.3 and the bottleneck brief only note that epoch blocks run unpipelined (538 vs 358 ms, 'executing->done'), which excludes the ~0.5 s barrier gap.

What changed since boundaries were made serial (exec-pipeline design, Aug):
- That design assumed bench epoch_length 100,000. Bench and testnet now use 100: devnet/wsl, testnet/genesis-weighted-base.json, and the hsdb-a-46428bfa worktree's generated genesis-3val.json.
- Phase 3 made every barrier a forced synchronous checkpoint drain (app.rs:2381-2387), about 10x the old wait_idle-only barrier.
- Bug (b) (732c78ed) removed the consensus-thread staking writer behind F8.

No collision with Phase 5 (it does not touch the pipelined predicate) or the s123 branches. app.rs is shared with item 7, which keeps `!has_evm` serial, and with propose-defer, in a different area.
candidates.regime: 300m exec-bound (primary); 10m at tail depth 4 (secondary); 10m at depth 1 about 0 (exec not the limit)
candidates.risks:
1. Liveness at boundary H+L. The plan stored at H becomes durable only when the async %100 checkpoint lands. The margin is about 34 or more blocks (queue at most 66, L = 100); the worst case is a refused and retried boundary proposal.
2. The fast path at a boundary is untested today. The existing %100 pipelined test uses epoch_length 1000, so the differential test above is required.
3. The F8 audit should be redone after bug (b): check that no other consensus-thread or RPC reader of CF_STAKING_* or epoch rows assumes the boundary is durable when it executes. Candidates are the async-validate validator count, the leader state and the state-hash submitter, which reads `durable`.
4. The gain scales with epochs per second. It holds for epoch_length 100 (bench and testnet); a long mainnet epoch shrinks it.
5. If the %100 checkpoint falls under 2 s after an interval checkpoint, the exec thread waits in checkpoint_submit. That wait is bounded by and smaller than today's barrier, so never worse.
6. A one-line conflict surface with item 7 in app.rs, which is unpushed on 18c.

Every serial block pays the same barrier: an EVM tx, a slash or an epoch boundary each force a synchronous checkpoint drain, about 0.5 s at 300m, plus about 0.12 s of serial flush. item7-evm-lanes.md:88-90 sizes the serial-block cost from 'executing->done' spans, which exclude the barrier. Measurement artifact: 120 s cells contain 4-6 epoch barriers, each worth about 0.4-0.5% of the cell. This is a hidden source of noise in 120 s A/Bs.

result.notes:
I found two candidates. Both move or cut serial exec-thread work on the per-order path into the book. Together they are worth an estimated -12 to -17 ms per native block at 300m, about 4-5% of the 313 ms exec wall.

Data basis and caveats:
- The newest call-graph profile is d3cba5e2 (300m, val1, W1, cycles:u at 499 Hz, files /home/oz/bench-results-matched/ozarchy-p4s0-run/analyst/p{1,2}-mperf-w1-*.script.gz). I diffed both code regions against main a44000e0; they are unchanged apart from cloid fix 3 and a typed-load parameter.
- Exec-thread numbers are robust: two independent profiles agree to within 0.3 percentage points.
- Pool-thread sample counts are approximate. Threads that wake often can be biased under -F (memory 68626b6b). I used pool numbers only to bound the match-phase dilution.
- I wrote the analysis helpers to /tmp/ob-research. No cargo, bench or profiler was run.

Checked and not proposed:
1. **Classic book journals.** row_journal and level_journal BTreeSet inserts are discarded in Classic mode (native_executor.rs:6276-6278). They cost 3.3% of pool CPU (match_at_level and insert_order) plus 0.9% of exec CPU (discard). Skipping them would conflict with Phase 5 step 3, which builds Classic rows from a book dirty set at the same sites.
2. **Reduce-only sweep.** After every placement with fills, the sweep machinery (a touched BTreeSet<Address>, sweep_reduce_only per trader, and an order_index probe per fill) runs even when reduce_only_index is empty. That is 2.7% of pool CPU. Smaller trims: one eager order_seq.get per fill for mark_chunk_dirty while chunked mode is off, and rehash of AccountMargins.traders and the MAKER_FREE map. Together these are about 4-5% of pool CPU: about -1% CPU-s/1M and under +0.5% matched/s. Too weak to propose alone.
3. **Cancel-all locate.** The plan's partition_point does an order_seq hash probe per binary-search step: 2.4% of exec on-CPU (sec 25.1 'locate' 9.7 ms on 707f132f). With only 5 levels per side at band 5, one linear pass per level could halve it. But the s123 parallel cancel-all branch moves this work to the pool, so its standalone value is about 1%. It is complementary (torus-core only, read-only plan), so revisit after that branch.
4. **Maker account snapshot.** maker_account (AccountReader::get_position binary search plus maker_free per worker) is about 17% of match CPU. It belongs to Users-layout and Phase 5 territory.
5. **Smaller exec-thread items.** Post-match TraderMarkets::absorb (1%), MatchResult drops on the exec thread (0.9%) and record_margin_cuts (0.3%) are each 1-2.5 ms per block. Possible riders, not candidates.

candidates.title: Split the exec-pool match and pass-A work into K jobs per worker so threads that start late do not hold back the phase, and optionally let the exec thread run jobs too
candidates.mechanism: Today match and settle pass A cut their markets into exactly as many LPT chunks as there are workers (min(cap, markets) = 32 at 300m). On a 32-thread host shared by 3 nodes, the 32 woken pool threads start their single chunk anywhere from 0 to about 8 ms after the phase begins, because they wait for a CPU. The chunks hold equal work, so a phase ends only when the latest starter finishes. Threads that start early go idle while late starters are still working. Proposed change, behind TORUS_EXEC_POOL_GRAIN=K: make min(markets, K x cap) LPT chunks but keep the same pool size, so early-running workers steal the extra chunks through rayon's existing scope work-stealing. The phase then ends at about total work / concurrency plus one small chunk. Optional sub-flag TORUS_EXEC_POOL_CALLER=1: run_jobs uses pool.in_place_scope plus an atomic cursor, so the exec thread, which is already on a CPU, processes chunks right away instead of blocking on a LockLatch. That also removes the exec-to-worker start latency and most of the end wake-up, which together measured about 1 to 1.7 ms per phase. Scheduling only: every chunk's result comes back by market id or input index, and the per-market computations are independent. State stays byte-identical.

candidates.title: Run the gossip-verify and ingress-verify pools at nice +N so the exec thread, the exec pool and the checkpoint helper threads win the CPU on the shared host
candidates.mechanism:
At 300m every node's exec thread is the bottleneck and every pool phase is on its critical path. Yet the host is oversubscribed in bursts, and two things push the critical threads down:
- The kernel is BORE (sched_bore=1, penalty offset 24, scale 1536). Tasks whose CPU bursts exceed about 17 ms lose priority. The exec thread runs 60-125 ms between sleeps, so it competes at roughly nice +3..+6 (inference from the BORE formula, not measured).
- The 2 x 16 verify threads per node (1.7-1.8 cores per node, about 5.3 cores fleet-wide) run short jobs and keep full weight. They preempt the exec thread and the exec-pool workers, and they share CPUs with them.

The candidate: setpriority(PRIO_PROCESS, gettid(), N) in each verify pool's rayon start_handler. Raising nice is allowed unprivileged, and Linux nice is per thread. A secondary sub-flag uses RocksDB's own Env::lower_thread_pool_cpu_priority for the LOW (compaction) pool.

With N=10 the bulk threads drop well below the exec thread even after its BORE penalty. The exec thread, pool workers, ckpt-merge, end-resident and hotstuff-algo then preempt bulk work instead of waiting behind it. Bulk work still uses the roughly 40% idle CPU. Unlike pinning or bounded pools, no capacity is removed.

The set is limited on purpose. Unchanged: the exec pool, the global rayon pool (exec phase-1 verify and the consensus validate path), tokio (networking) and rpc-worker (it serves the bench commit tail at 10m).

result.notes:
Lens: locks, thread pools, scheduling and tail stalls. Main a44000e0, read-only. Analysis used only existing artifacts; nothing was run. Two candidates, best first.

Checked and dropped, with numbers:
- **Lock contention on the exec critical path is negligible.**
  - BlockSums/BatchSums memo Mutex and OnceLock: 0.16-0.21% of exec wall (p4s0 step0-table.txt).
  - Overlay RwLock (is_read_lockable): about 1% of pool CPU (cloidec prof-B).
  - Exec-thread kernel time: 0.6% of its samples (p4s0 W1).
  - Trust-cache RwLock<FifoCache>: read-only lookups, trivial write holds.
- **Rayon idle spin is small on current main.** The 32 global-pool namesake threads ("torus-execution" non-main) use 0.025 cores per node (hsdb io-threads). The large sched_yield share seen in the p4s0 perf window is inflated by perf. The exec pool's sys share is 2-3%.
- **Mempool write-lock convoy among verify threads is real but off the 300m critical path.** Verify threads were blocked 1.84 s/s in submit_native_action_inner (p4j3 off-CPU). The consensus thread's select/remove_committed means are 18-21 ms and 7 ms.
- **Exec queue handoff, flush handoff (0.01 ms) and end-resident wait (0.3 ms) are negligible.**
- **ckpt-merge spawns a fresh thread per block** (app.rs:359-386). Settle wait is 8.5-9.4 ms per block, but it scales with layer size (3.7-4.2 ms in 120 s cells), so it is merge work. defer-book-blobs (AVOID) covers it.
- **THP:** defrag=madvise; compact_stall 716 in 23 h.
- **Shrinking pools (fewer exec-pool threads) is not proposed.** It conflicts with the refuted bounded-pools (-67.7%) and SAVE_BOOKS_WORKERS=4 (-34%).
- **Exec verify phase 1** (global-pool par_iter with about 100% hits): left alone. It is the s123 exec-action-keys-parallel area and the "tiny gain" revisit item.

**Data caveat:** the pool timeline evidence comes from d3cba5e2 (P2-3 pool and the same chunking as main) recorded under perf. Re-check the start skew on main with a cheap per-phase timer before the A/B.

**Order:** the two candidates overlap on the pool phases. A/B exec-pool-fine-grain-jobs first, then bulk-thread-nice on top.

**Analysis scripts:** /tmp/torus-explore/{pooltl,phases,gaps,startend,disp,model,thr,hist,kern,grp,excats}.py.

**Memory saved:** project:torus-hyperbft, lens:locks-pools-scheduling (exec-pool start skew, run-delay and preemption data, BORE premise).

candidates.title: Serialize the Classic book blobs on the exec pool, into presized buffers, instead of one at a time on the exec thread
candidates.mechanism:
Classic is the book mode on the bench and on testnet. In it, save_order_books (native_executor.rs:6252-6279) runs borsh::to_vec(&book) for every dirty market, one after another, on the exec thread. Each Vec starts at 1 KiB and grows by doubling. The blob then goes in with put_cf_raw_owned, and the book's row and level journals are thrown away. Modes 2/3 already save in parallel (drain_books_parallel, :2864-2925), but Classic never takes that path (:6245-6251 sets last_save_workers = 1).

With TORUS_PARALLEL_BOOK_SAVE=N, N >= 2:
1. Take &mut handles to the dirty books in one iter_mut pass, sorted by market id, exactly as drain_level_books does.
2. Each book becomes one work item on the exec pool, heaviest first. The item computes the exact serialized length in a pre-pass (Order is 97 B, +16 B with a cloid, +16 or +32 B for stop types), allocates a Vec of that size, serializes into it, and drops the book's journals.
3. Back on the exec thread, put_cf_raw_owned runs in ascending market order with today's fault latching and logging, followed by the order-id counter and mode-marker writes.

Optional sub-flag: Classic books stop keeping the row and level journals at all (journal sites in torus-core order_book.rs:2117-3102). Today every block builds them and save throws them away.

candidates.title: Hand out per-market work items dynamically (heaviest first, exec thread joins) instead of one static LPT chunk per pool thread
candidates.mechanism:
exec_pool::run_jobs (exec_pool.rs:43-59) runs one job per static LPT chunk. The chunk count equals the worker cap, which equals the pool size (32 per node on archy): match at market_workers.rs:146-151 and 208-222; pass A at native_executor.rs:8672-8701 via settle_worker_cap at :579-583. Meanwhile the exec thread blocks inside pool().scope.

With 3 nodes sharing 32 hardware threads, pool threads wake and run at uneven times. A late or preempted thread holds its whole chunk, so the phase ends long after most threads have gone idle.

With TORUS_EXEC_POOL_DYNAMIC=1, a new helper `exec_pool::run_items_dynamic` does this:
1. Hand out per-market items from an AtomicUsize cursor, heaviest first, using the same weights as today: request count for match, orders + 2 x fills for pass A.
2. Run inside ThreadPool::in_place_scope (rayon-core 1.13.0). The exec thread starts on items at t=0 and up to cap-1 pool helpers join as they wake.
3. Store results by item index: match results are re-sorted by market id as today, pass A plans by index.

Use it for match and pass A, and for the parallel book save and the s123 cancel-all pass if they are adopted.

candidates.title: Send hash manifests instead of full-body pre-proposal pushes (gossip pre-spread already delivers every body)
candidates.mechanism:
Each body now reaches every validator twice. Native gossip pre-spread is on by default (torus-node main.rs:180-192), and the bench env also pins TORUS_HASH_ONLY_PUSH_THRESHOLD=8000000 (devnet/wsl/env.sh:45; the compiled production default is 512 KB at bridge.rs:97), so every leader also pushes the full bincode body set (~5 MB, 390 actions) to both followers.

What each pushed copy costs:
- Leader: serialize, then a per-peer borsh copy and zstd compress.
- Follower, on the swarm loop: zstd decompress and a bincode decode of the whole batch (swarm.rs:1661-1679).
- Then add_native_action_from_gossip runs on the gossip-verify pool and does all of this BEFORE it finds the duplicate (mempool lib.rs:792-835, 1351-1379; native_pool.rs:414-426):
  - mirror_to_da: a deep clone, then put_batch (compute_action_hash + bincode serialize + a RocksDB put);
  - verified_cache_key (a canonical-bytes Keccak);
  - a pool write lock, plus compute_action_hash and serialized_size under that lock.

With a hash manifest (0xFC, ~12.8 KB), followers run plan_prewarm_requests (swarm.rs:2610-2646): they check DA presence and pull only the missing bodies, from the proposer, on the off-loop serve path. That is the design the CLI doc describes: 'compact proposals need only gap-pulls'.

Step 1 needs no code (an A/B of the existing knob). Optional step 2:
- 2a: reuse the leader's already-computed native_hashes in the bundle and skip the deep clone in mirror_or_drop_native (app.rs:6628-6629).
- 2b: if the owner keeps the full push as a WAN safety net, return Duplicate before mirror and Keccak work whenever (sender, nonce) is pooled with identical canonical bytes.
candidates.evidence:
Main-code 300m 600 s cells (ozarchy-hsdb-300m-r2-B, crates byte-identical to a44000e0).

Push volume, from the 'received pre-proposal action batch' and 'pre-proposal FULL-BODY push' log lines:
- Each node receives 1,202-1,206 full-body batches per cell = 468-471k actions (avg 390 actions, 4.9-5.6 MB). There are 0 manifests.
- Direct-path zstd counter: 5.7-6.5 GB pre-compression vs 0.47-0.54 GB on the wire per node.

Redundancy:
- Every pushed action is also delivered by gossip or by the node's own RPC (val1):
  - trust-cache misses 471,202 = native gossip received 471,199;
  - hits 1,177,549 = 470,627 push copies + ~706.9k exec lookups.
  So the ~470k push copies per node are duplicate ingests.
- The push can only beat gossip when the leader picks its own RPC-admitted action within the 50 ms gossip batch window (NATIVE_BATCH_INTERVAL_MS, swarm.rs:660). Order age at commit is under 0.32 s for only 0.68% of actions (histogram).

DA write amplification:
- DA puts per node = 235.5k RPC + 471.2k gossip + 470.6k push = 1.18M for 707k distinct actions. Push duplicates are ~40% of consensus-DB WAL bytes (25 MB/s).
- rocksdb-consensus-LOG: 934k cf_native_pending entries flushed (~244k duplicates collapsed in memtables) and 216k dropped by compaction, so ~24% of flushed DA entries are duplicates.

CPU, from p3cloidprof 300m val1 folded stacks:
- mirror_to_da 0.344 ms/1k fills (half is duplicates);
- verified_cache_key encode 0.116, admit/insert 0.114-0.138, decode_pre_proposal_batch 0.049, zstd 0.107 ms/1k.
- Keccak: a duplicate costs 3 x ~122 Keccak permutations (16.4 KB canonical bytes) vs ~1,666 for a first copy (1,200 EIP-712 item hashes + 95 + 3 x 122). That is ~18% of gossip-verify Keccak (2.19 ms/1k).
- gossip-verify uses 0.94-0.97 cores/node (io-threads).

10m is the same (p4tail10 a1/a4: direct pre 3.5-4.1 GB per node per 300 s cell).

History:
- s297 made the unicast push the delivery path while gossip was off.
- r4 raised the bench floor to 8 MB to avoid manifests, with no manifest-vs-push A/B. r3 cap300 ran ~45 manifests per node with 0 exhausted or starved.
candidates.determinism:
Transport-only and node-local. Receivers handle both 0xFD and 0xFC whatever the proposer chose (bridge.rs:99-106 documents per-node A/B safety).

Bodies still reach the DA store via gossip, RPC or the pre-warm and hot-path pulls before vote-after-body. Block contents and state are unchanged, so AGREE must hold.

Step 1 is an existing knob at its compiled production default. Step 2 flags would default off, with off identical to main.
candidates.flag:
Step 1: TORUS_HASH_ONLY_PUSH_THRESHOLD=512000 (existing knob at its compiled production default; the bench env pins 8000000). Optional third arm: 0.
Optional step 2, new flag, default off: TORUS_PUSH_MANIFEST_HASHES=1 (reuse native_hashes, skip the leader clone).
candidates.impl_size: Step 1: zero code. Step 2: S (~30-60 lines in app.rs PreProposalBundle, bridge.rs and mempool, plus tests).
candidates.risks:
- WAN robustness: S388 shows a follower whose gossip mesh is broken pulls every body from the proposer. Production at 512 KB already behaves this way; keep the override, or take step 2b, if the WAN safety net matters.
- Actions the leader selects within ~50 ms of its own RPC admission may be missing at followers. They are then pre-warm pulled (1 RTT, off-loop serve), with a small vote-delay bump on those views.
- plan_prewarm_requests does ~390 RocksDB point gets on the swarm loop per manifest (~2-4 ms), still less than today's ~5.5 ms batch decode. Bodies still in da_pending (<=50 ms or 128 bodies) read as missing and are pulled needlessly.
- Manifests are not retained for the T4 re-push on reconnect (rejoin cells).
- The gain is CPU and I/O; matched/s will likely tie.

Flag off is identical to main. Blob references stay readable if the node later reopens with the flag off; enable_blob_files only governs new writes (verify with a reopen test).

candidates.title: torus_getBlockBody: serialize each action straight to JSON (RawValue) instead of building a serde_json::Value tree
candidates.mechanism:
get_block_body (torus-rpc torus.rs:1788-1872) decodes the bincode body record. It then builds `serde_json::to_value(a)` for every action into `Vec<serde_json::Value>` (types.rs:750): a full IndexMap/Value tree for ~160k orders in a full 400-action body. jsonrpsee then walks that tree to produce the response string.

Under TORUS_RPC_BODY_RAW_JSON=1, each action is serialized once with serde_json::value::to_raw_value. torus-rpc already enables the raw_value feature (Cargo.toml:20). The response then embeds Box<RawValue> items, which skips the per-order map, key-string and Value allocations and their drops.

serde_json is built with preserve_order (indexmap is in its Cargo.lock dependencies), so the output bytes are identical to today's for every in-range value. The bench tail parses only nonce, signature and status (tools/bench-throughput/src/in_flight.rs:146-189).
candidates.evidence:
Section 70.5 (results doc lines 10070-10076): val2 CPU minus mean(val0, val1) = 189.7-198.8 ms per 400 actions the tail releases, ~85% of the ~226 ms the tail spends per full body. The handler re-serializes every action to JSON.

hsdb-300m-r2-B io-threads (main code): val2 rpc-worker 0.796 cores vs 0.170/0.172 on val0/val1. That +0.63 cores ≈ 3.1 bodies/s x ~190 ms.

Section 70.7: giving the tail 4x read capacity (depth 4) at 10m gave +4.49% (node A) / +6.52% (node B) matched/s; waves vanished and exec busy went from 0.77 to 0.99. Owner s121 (memory 8f9f6962) shelved the harness change.

Code: `.map(|a| serde_json::to_value(a).unwrap_or_default())` at torus.rs:1800-1804.
candidates.est_gain:
Expected serve cost per full body ~190 -> ~60-90 ms (2-3x; to be confirmed by microbench).

- 300m: val2 -0.3 to -0.45 cores, so fleet-mean CPU-s/1M -2 to -2.8%. matched/s about 0 (the tail already keeps up: lag p50 1).
- 10m tail depth 1 (the standard gate shape): tail capacity ~1,770 -> ~4,000+ actions/s vs ~1,500 needed. That removes most of the tail pacing, so I expect most of the depth-4 gain: +2 to +5% matched/s, an effect of the harness pacing, as in 70.5/70.7.
candidates.determinism:
RPC response encoding only. No consensus, state or exec path changes. Flag off is identical.

Flag on is byte-identical for realistic data. The only difference is for i128/u128 values outside the 64-bit range: today to_value fails there and unwrap_or_default emits null for the whole action, while the raw path emits the number.
candidates.flag: TORUS_RPC_BODY_RAW_JSON=1 (new, default off)
candidates.impl_size: S: ~40-60 lines (a second field representation or custom Serialize for native_actions) plus tests.
candidates.test_plan:

Microbench: serve a 400x400-order body both ways, plus a jsonrpsee round trip.

Bench:

- 300m 600 s n=3.

Metrics: val2 rpc-worker CPU per body (io-threads), taillag.json lag p50/p99, per-wave idle (70.5 waves.py), matched/s, native blk/s, CPU-s/1M, AGREE. Watch 300m matched/s for closed-loop effects.
candidates.novelty_check:

No memory, branch or commit proposes a cheaper getBlockBody encoding (searched for getBlockBody, RawValue, to_value and body JSON; git log --all). The s120 audit (memory 71a4d9e8) only listed the JSON re-serialize as the serve path.

Not in any AVOID item. It overlaps the RPC lens, which may report it too.

- A faster tail can change the 300m closed loop (70.7 saw -5.2% at 300m depth 4, n=1), so measure 300m.

result.notes:
I found 3 candidates (ranked best first), all from main a44000e0 code and the ozarchy-hsdb-300m-r2-B cells, which run the same code as main. I ran no cargo, benches or profilers; I only read logs and saved metrics.

1. **Why the latency side of this lens doesn't convert to throughput now.** At 300m the view takes 315 ms, the same as exec block_ms (313). Proposal arrival on val0/val1 is ~160 ms because leaders sit in the blocking exec send. On the follower:
   - validate_block is ~9 ms, of which DA reconstruct is 9.5 ms;
   - vote delay is ~20 ms;
   - insert_persist is ~27 ms.
   
   So cutting time between proposal and vote, or the DA decode, is hidden by exec back-pressure. At 10m, tail depth 1 is limited by the bench's tail and depth 4 is exec-bound. What this lens can actually change is CPU and disk on the shared host, which is what candidates 1 and 2 target. Candidate 3 is a body-serialization fix that also removes the 10m tail pacing.

2. **Rejected or not proposed:**
   - **TORUS_BODY_PUSH_MAX_BYTES=65536.** This knob already exists. One thing has changed since July: because a follower now votes only after it holds the body (s84), the body-fetch round trip now sits before the vote. Even so, the July result still holds: loaded views are paced by exec, so it would be neutral.
   - **Pool-clone reconstruct instead of a DA decode.** This is too close to next-leader-parent-path-slim, which was refuted.
   - **Turning off gossipsub message signing.** This is a protocol change, not node-local.
   - **QUIC and UDP tuning.** The 8 MB UDP buffer was already tried with no gain.
   - **Duplicate short-circuit at gossip ingest.** This is folded into candidate 1 as step 2b.

3. **Side finding outside this lens (build flag, not env-flaggable).** RocksDB computes the WAL CRC32C with the portable table code (DefaultCRC32):
   - In the p3cloidprof 300m profile, 0.573 ms per 1k fills (~0.13 cores per node) sits under DBImpl::WriteToWAL → log::Writer::AddRecord.
   - The cause: librocksdb-sys build.rs adds -msse4.2/-mpclmul only when rustc target features include them, and the bench build.sh RUSTFLAGS has no target-feature or target-cpu setting. SST checksums default to XXH3, so this cost is WAL only.
   - Inferred, not measured: at ~0.5-0.6 GB/s, the ~200 MB checkpoint batch would spend ~0.3 s of its ~0.6 s DB write on CRC while it holds the state-DB write group. That points at the in-window p99 (sec 74.6) and at CPU-s/1M (about -2.4%).
   - Suggest routing this to the state/RocksDB lens or to 18c's checkpoint-slicing work. Test: rebuild with RUSTFLAGS '+sse4.2,+pclmulqdq' and microbench a 200 MB WriteBatch. It belongs to the shelved 'release profile tuning' item.

4. **Production storage issue:** cf_native_pending is never pruned. It flushes ~1.8 GB per node per 10 min at 300m, and its compaction cost grows with it. A retention or prune design (or FIFO compaction with a large cap) is a follow-up for 18c; candidate 2 removes the CPU and I/O part but not the disk growth.

5. **Combined effect if 1 and 2 both land:** about -0.35 cores per node, so CPU-s/1M about -6 to -8%, and device writes about -25 MB/s per node. All three candidates are node-local, leave consensus and state untouched, and must keep AGREE in every cell.

Memory saved: project:torus-hyperbft, type:learning (DA/network lens numbers).

candidates.title: Integrated BlobDB for the DA body CF (cf_native_pending) so compaction stops rewriting ~14 KB action bodies
candidates.mechanism: The DA store writes every admitted native action into cf_native_pending in the consensus DB. Each value is a bincode SignedNativeAction: about 14 KB for a 400-order place, about 0.2 KB for a cancel. Keys are random 32-byte hashes. Nothing ever deletes these rows: NativeDaStore::remove has no production caller, and the RH4 GC exists only on origin/perf/p3-throughput 4077726a. The CF is only point-read (Get/MultiGet, no iterator). Leveled compaction over random keys therefore rewrites the whole value payload about 5x, with LZ4 to ZSTD each time: 53 GB uncompressed rewritten per 10 GB flushed per 600 s. The fix turns on RocksDB integrated BlobDB for this one CF: enable_blob_files, min_blob_size 4 KiB, blob_compression_type ZSTD, blob GC off because nothing is deleted. Values are then written once to blob files at flush, and compaction moves only keys plus small blob refs. WAL, memtable and the foreground put path do not change. Reads fetch the blob (page cache) instead of an SST data block. Optional second arm: the same options on cf_block_bodies (3.7 MB per height, about 15.5 s compaction plus 7 s flush per node per 600 s).

crates/torus-state/src/db.rs:360-380 and 682-696 (CONSENSUS_DB_CFS, consensus DB budgets, open_consensus)
crates/torus-state/src/native_da.rs:176-263 (get_batch_timed batched_multi_get_cf, missing, get_raw_batch, contains -> db.rs:1347-1350 get_pinned_cf; all keep working on blob values)

candidates.est_gain:
300m: CPU-s/1M down 0.73-0.88 (-3.1% to -3.8% of 23.38). It removes about 95% of the 116-125 CPU-s per node per 600 s, minus about 8-10 s extra for ZSTD (instead of LZ4) at flush and about 2 s of key-only compaction.

candidates.determinism: Changes only the on-disk layout of a node-local, non-hashed CF. Every Get/MultiGet returns byte-identical values, and consensus, the running state hash and AGREE never see the layout. With the flag off, options are exactly today's. Data dirs open in place both ways: RocksDB reads blob references without the option, and old inline SSTs migrate on their next compaction.
candidates.flag: TORUS_ROCKSDB_DA_BLOB=zstd|lz4 (unset = today; zstd keeps DA disk size about equal to today's bottommost ZSTD). Optional second arm: TORUS_ROCKSDB_BODY_BLOB for cf_block_bodies.
candidates.impl_size: small (about 40-60 lines in db.rs plus tests; no reader changes)
candidates.test_plan:
Tests first (torus-state):

- get / get_batch_timed / missing / contains / get_raw_batch return identical bytes and order, including duplicates and unsorted input.

- node_dbs reopen_recovers_hotstuff_state_and_da_bodies passes with the knob on.

Bench (archy, same binary):
- 300m, 600 s, ABBA n=3-4, arms unset vs zstd.
- Report CPU-s/1M (a 0.7% step resolved at n=3 in sec 74.1), consensus compaction CPU and bytes (expect about -95%), device MB/s per node, rocksdb:low thread CPU from io-threads, DA read timers (DaReadTiming multi_get), matched/s, blk/s, block p99, RSS, and the disk total including *.blob.
- AGREE in every cell.
- Optional 10m pair and a cf_block_bodies arm.
candidates.novelty_check:
Not in the AVOID list, the s123 survivors, or the 3 recovered refuted s123 candidates.
- The append-CF compaction plan (mem 0f55e61a) covered codec (TORUS_ROCKSDB_APPEND_CF_CODEC LZ4: off, not clearly better), WAL cap, universal compaction (in reserve) and WAL compression. It never covered blob files.
- A sibling DA/network lens of this same round (mem 873b7f65) also notes 'no BlobDB ever tried': merge with that finding, not prior work.
- The s123 storage lens's rejected candidates were not recovered by name, so 18c should confirm it was not among the 11 unnamed ones.
- No collision with checkpoint slicing, defer-books, item 7 or Phase 5 (consensus-DB per-CF options only).
candidates.regime: 300m and 10m (DA bytes scale with actions, not markets); larger on long-running nodes
candidates.risks:
- Blob files never get deleted while DA is never pruned. About 115 new blob files per node per 600 s, all kept open (max_open_files -1; nofile limit is 524288) plus MANIFEST growth. Pair it later with DA retention (RH4 port) plus blob GC.

- Reads of flushed bodies now cost one pread plus decompress per blob (no blob cache). The consensus-thread reconstruct and proposer missing() calls mostly hit the memtable. Watch the DA read timers.

candidates.title: Stop deep-copying CF_NATIVE_POSITIONS into the per-block ingress-view slices (RSS -0.3 to -0.5 GB at 300m)
candidates.mechanism:
Phase 3 step 2 publishes a ReadView that layers 8 ingress CFs over the DB.
- For every block since the last checkpoint (about 40 at 300m), the per-block merge thread deep-copies the block's ingress CFs into a slice (FrozenPending::slice -> BTreeMap clone_from).
- The view keeps all of them until the checkpoint. There E hands about 40 slices to a 2-slot dropper and frees about 37 of them inline on the exec thread.
- CF_NATIVE_POSITIONS is about 92% of these entries (139 B each).

The only reader of positions through the view is funded::is_funded's third fallback (anti-spam item A, an 'any open position' prefix seek). It runs only after the perp-collateral and spot checks fail. Item A is off on the bench devnet (TORUS_INGRESS_MIN_COLLATERAL=0). The RPC verify path reads only markets and sessions, and addr-rate reads cum volume from CF_NATIVE_BALANCES.

Simple variant: the flag removes CF_NATIVE_POSITIONS from one ingress_cfs() table used by both the slicer (app.rs:382) and ReadView::layered. Positions are then neither copied nor layered, and a view read of positions goes to the DB.

Production-safe variant (for item A on): per block, keep only the distinct trader prefixes that had a position write or tombstone (at most 5k addresses). Fallback 3 answers 'funded' for those traders and asks the DB for the rest. This never refuses anyone main admits; it can admit a trader who closed everything within the window, for at most one interval.

result.notes:
Lens: state write path, RocksDB and checkpointing on main a44000e0. Read-only; no cargo or bench was run. Memory saved (project:torus-hyperbft). Two candidates passed the self-checks; I found no exec-thread lever in this lens that is above noise and not already on the AVOID list.

Considered and rejected:
- **unordered_write on the state DB** (for the in-window p99): small writers would still wait for the 200 MB batch's WAL write (~35-40% of the 0.6 s). It requires turning pipelined writes off. It also breaks snapshot immutability for non-ingress DB readers, such as the R24 per-book snapshots in level-row modes. It targets the same stall as slicing, which is in flight, and does it worse.
- **WAL-off for the checkpoint batch** (revisit item): besides atomic_flush (the r9 finding), it needs a forced memtable flush before any later WAL'd write that carries the applied marker. Serial EVM blocks are such writes, and without the barrier the marker recovers ahead of the lost checkpoint, which is a fork. It sits on the same code slicing is rewriting; revisit after slicing lands.
- **Positions CF compaction tuning** (L0 trigger 8, no L0 compression): at most ~0.05 CPU-s/1M. Positions flush plus compaction is only ~40 CPU-s per node per 600 s.
- **Memtable insert hints** are not in the C API. A **vector memtable** sorts on every Get or iterator.
- **State-DB block cache** usage is 87 bytes at cell end, so cache size is no RSS lever.
- **Checkpoint-block inline merges on the exec thread** (2 block merges plus slice frees, upkeep 25-205 ms at checkpoint blocks): average ~1 ms per block, so below matched/s noise. Mostly covered by candidate 2.

One more finding that cannot be an env flag: librocksdb-sys gets -msse4.2/-mpclmul only from rustc target features, and .cargo/config.toml sets none. RocksDB therefore uses software CRC32C for every WAL record (including the ~200 MB checkpoint batch, lengthening the write window) and for every SST block. This is a build-flag change for 18c and the release-profile item. The sibling DA lens (mem 873b7f65) found it too.

Candidate 1 overlaps that same sibling lens's DA-compaction observation; merge the two. Its DA push-dedup candidate complements candidate 1. The unmerged RH4 DA GC (origin/perf/p3-throughput 4077726a) is related prior work: DA is still never pruned on main.

candidates.title: Settle pass B: write per-order results in one tight scatter after the market loop instead of one cache miss per order (plus optional off-thread drop of match results)
candidates.mechanism:
In the parallel settle's pass B (the serial apply loop, markets in ascending id), every prepared order ends with `results[prep.index] = NativeActionResult::placed(result)` (native_executor.rs:8904).
- `results` has one 56-byte entry per flattened order: about 95k entries, ~5.3 MB per native block on main.
- It is filled with "pending" placeholders at :7250, long before settle runs.
- Pass B walks orders market by market, so consecutive writes jump about 300 slots (~17 KB). Every write lands on a cold cache line.
- The assignment first runs NativeActionResult's drop glue, which loads the old `Option<Cow<str>>` niche word. That load misses.
- Each pass-B iteration is a long chain of work (balance-cache load/set, persist_trade, metric atomics), so only one miss is in flight at a time. About 90-110 ns is exposed per order.

Fix, behind a flag:
- Inside the loop, push `(prep.index as u32, result.reject)` into a pre-sized sequential Vec (8 bytes per order). `placed()` depends only on `reject`, and FailureReason is Copy.
- After the market loop, write the identical `NativeActionResult` values in a tight scatter loop. That loop has many misses in flight, so the cost drops to well under 1 ms.
- The rare fill-failure write (:8874-8883) stays inline.
- Apply the same change to the sequential settle (:8509).

Optional second part (separate sub-flag): the end-of-iteration drop of each market's `Vec<MatchResult>` (and of `plan.orders`, if the zip iterates by reference) frees ~95k small Vecs on the exec thread. Hand them to a background dropper instead, the same pattern as app.rs `Dropper` / torus-ckpt-drop.

candidates.title: Remove scattered PreparedOrder / params loads from three serial exec-thread loops: sell_top_ups, the s92 margin-cut counters and the Phase-3 match-request build
candidates.mechanism:
C2 made PreparedOrder borrow `params` from the block's action list, so no per-order clone is made. Three serial exec-thread loops then visit orders in market-major order and load scattered memory per order:

(a) sell_top_ups (:9858-9920). Main has 44.4k full top-ups per native block. The function collects (index, market, k), sorts it, then reads `market_batches[m][k]` (a random 176-byte PreparedOrder) and `p.params.quantity`, which is a second random line.

(b) The s92 counter loop after matching (:7787-7795). For every order it reads `p.params.is_buy` and does two atomic inc_by. On the bench the counters it feeds stay 0.

(c) The Phase-3 MatchRequest build (:7701-7710). For each checked taker, `taker_margin_limit` reads params.order_type, time_in_force and price, plus an Arc clone of the tiers.

Fix, behind a flag:
(a) stitch_outcome (:8190) runs in flat order on both the serial and the sharded prepare paths, and params is hot there. It appends each top-up candidate (index, market, k, sender, quantity, margin_reserved) to a sequential list. sell_top_ups walks that list in order, with no sort and no PreparedOrder or params reads, keeping the same bal_cache trajectory. Grants (market, k, grant, full) are applied afterwards in a tight loop. Fallback if stitch should stay untouched: gather the same tuple while iterating each market's Vec sequentially.
(b) Test `r.result.margin_cut_price.is_some()` before touching params. Sum maker_margin_cancels and reduce_only_cuts per market and call inc_by once per market.
(c) Carry `margin_reserved: Option<FixedPoint>` in MatchRequest, plus the market's tiers once per batch. match_market then builds TakerMarginLimit on the pool worker with the same function. The worker already reads params (req.params.clone(), market_workers.rs:351/359).

candidates.title: 4-way AVX2 Keccak for the 400 per-order EIP-712 item hashes in hash_place_order_batch, the dominant verify-thread CPU
candidates.mechanism:
Verifying a 400-order PlaceOrderBatch hashes each order as an EIP-712 item.
- Each item is the 32-byte typehash plus 9 fields of 32 bytes: a fixed 320-byte preimage, 3 Keccak-f[1600] permutations (eip712.rs:311-354).
- That makes 1,200 permutations per action, against ~95 for the item-hash concatenation and ~130 for each canonical-bytes key or hash. So ~78% of verify-thread Keccak is item hashing.
- The items are independent and equal-length, which fits multi-buffer SIMD exactly.

Fix, behind a flag:
- Add Keccak-256 x4 for fixed 320-byte inputs, using an AVX2 4-lane state type.
- The keccak 0.1.6 crate already in Cargo.lock exposes a generic `keccak_p<L: LaneSize>` over a public `LaneSize` trait. Its own `simd` feature needs nightly portable_simd; the toolchain is stable 1.98.1. So write a `[u64;4]` newtype lane, or copy the ~60-line round loop, inside a `#[target_feature(enable="avx2")]` function, guarded by `is_x86_feature_detected!`.
- Use it in hash_place_order_batch (:363) for groups of 4 items; keep the scalar alloy keccak256 for the remainder and for everything else.

All callers reach this function through eip712_struct_hash: gossip recover, RPC ingress verify, and exec-time recover on a trust-cache miss.

result.notes:
I found three new candidates; none overlaps the prior-work brief.

**Method.** Read-only. No cargo, perf record or bench was run. I parsed the existing perf-script dumps with Python scripts in /tmp/claude-explore-prof (inl.py, drill.py, w2.py, w2sites.py). For the W2 data, sample addresses were mapped through a2l-cache.json after recovering the load base by matching the low 12 bits of the keys. Stalled instructions were identified with objdump on the archived d3cba5e2 node binary.

**Caveat on the data.** Every exec-thread profile with stacks comes from a pre-Phase-4 build: d3cba5e2 (p4s0, 300m), ef812b02 (p3cloidprof W2, exec-only, 5 events, 6 cells) and c88d3073 (prof-B). For candidates 1 and 2 I confirmed the code at the cited sites is unchanged on a44000e0. One cycles:u profile on head would confirm the shares before an A/B, but it is not required.

**Thread ranking, current main 300m 600 s** (hsdb-300m-r2-B io-threads, per node):

| Thread group | Cores per node | Share |
|---|---|---|
| exec-pool | 1.13-1.16 | ~22% |
| gossip-verify | 0.94-0.97 | ~18% |
| exec thread | 0.85 | ~16% |
| ingress-verify | 0.76-0.84 | ~15% |
| tokio | 0.44 (sys 23%) | ~8% |
| rocksdb:low | 0.26-0.28 | ~5% |
| hotstuff | 0.18 | ~3.5% |
| rpc-worker | 0.17 (val2: 0.80) | — |

**Function ranking.**
- Node level: Keccak is 19.8% at 300m (c88d3073) and 24.4% at 10m (Phase 4). k256 ecrecover is about 7-10%.
- Exec thread, unaddressed: the pass-B results store (~3.5%), sell_top_ups (2-6%), the s92 counter loop (1-1.3%) and the MatchRequest build (0.7-1%).
- Exec thread, already covered: cancel-all (s123 #1), cache flush and save_books (Phase 5), verify and sort keccak (s123 #3), liquidations in the post-engine tail (Phase 5; liq-scan refuted), prepare_one (TORUS_PARALLEL_ENGINE A/B). The post_engine_tail of 11.9 ms is mostly run_liquidations.

**Weaker leads I did not promote:**
- **libsecp256k1 backend for ecrecover.**
  - k256 recover is about 7-10% of node cycles, including constant-time select code that public-key recovery does not need. libsecp256k1 (the `secp256k1` crate, 0.30/0.31 already in Cargo.lock) is likely about 2x faster.
  - A node-local flag is only safe with exact edge-case parity with k256 (high-s, r/s range, recid).
  - It sits close to the AVOID item 'crypto tuning for ingress'. What has changed since: CPU-s/1M from cycles:u data, versus the s367 latency premise.
- **torus_getBlockBody.** It runs `serde_json::to_value` for each action and then serializes the Value tree (torus-rpc/src/torus.rs:1788-1866). Serving the bench tail costs val2 0.63 cores at 300m and 0.72 at 10m. `serde_json::value::to_raw_value` (the raw_value feature is already enabled) would avoid the Value tree, but the split between decode, to_value, FixedPoint formatting and HTTP is unmeasured; val2 needs a profile first. A 10m depth-1 matched/s gain is plausible but limited by the client-side parse.
- **Seeded fixed-width Address hasher.** Address hashing is about 3.6% of exec on-CPU and about 6.9% of pool samples (d3cba5e2): a length prefix plus hash_bytes_long for 20 bytes. Part of this is key-load stalls that candidate 2 removes.
- **users::find interpolation probe** (users.rs:1205). Each trader's positions are a sorted Vec of about 300 entries at 300m, so the market id predicts the index. Estimated around +1%: below noise.
- **The pool is host-contended.** Pool CPU is about 370 ms per native block against 42 ms of match plus pass_a wall, so pool CPU cuts shorten those phases on archy.

**Suggested order:**
- Candidates 1 and 2 can share one 300m ABBA n=4 campaign (2x2 or a combined arm).
- Candidate 3 should pass its microbench gate before any node A/B.
- All three edit native_executor.rs, torus-types or market_workers.rs: coordinate with Phase 5 step 2 (pass B) and the s123 cancel-all branch (market_workers.rs).
