   - Value 1: bench fidelity.
   - Value 2: evidence for the production threshold decision. bridge.rs:101-106 calls 512 KB 'likely too eager' pending a WAN test. This A/B puts a price of about 4% node CPU and about 15% of device writes on raising the threshold while gossip pre-spread is on.

2. Changing env.sh moves the CPU-s/1M (about -4%) and bytes-written (about -15%) baselines against sections 60-74. That is an owner call. If adopted, re-baseline and run both arms in the same campaign.

3. Only CPU-s/1M and bytes written can pass. matched/s, blk/s and block_ms will tie, so under the phase-gate template this is CPU/IO hygiene. Precedent: the LZ4 codec's CPU-only gain was kept off by default under the owner's 'only if clearly better' rule.

4. Guards. Past manifest/pull wedges (S387, S419, P3 c1324afa, e1bd7ad7) involved on-loop serving, serial verify, or oversized bodies; those fixes are now in. Still:
   - plan_prewarm_requests checks only RocksDB, so these read as missing and get pulled:

     - leader-RPC actions less than 50 ms old.

   - Watch: view_vote_delay, timeouts, validate_block_da_wait, native_da_served and serve_dropped, the pre-warm pull log lines, and AGREE in every cell.

   - Manifests are not kept for the T4 re-push on reconnect, which matters in rejoin cells.

5. A/B design:
   - 300m, 600 s, ABBA n=3-4; arms 8000000 vs 512000 on all 3 validators.
   - Primary: CPU-s/1M, io-threads (gossip-verify, tokio, rocksdb:low), consensus-DB wal/flush/compaction from sampler.csv, io-ticks.
   - Add one 10m pair.

6. Drop step 2a. Skipping the clone means restructuring the block-body build, and the clone costs only about 0.003 cores on hotstuff-algo, off the critical path. Hash reuse saves only about 0.01 cores.

7. If the owner keeps the full push as a WAN safety net, the merged duplicate is the code route. That is the gossip early dedup that returns Duplicate before the mirror, key and insert work. The premise holds on main a44000e0, and the gain recomputed from measured data is close to the candidate's. In the three hsdb-300m-r{1,2,3}-B cells (crates/ identical to main), every serial block is an epoch boundary: 27-28 per node over the whole log, all at h%100, and the bench genesis logs epoch_length=100. pipeline_barrier (app.rs:2377-2413) runs checkpoint_drain and then wait_idle on the exec thread. block_timer starts at app.rs:2965, before the barrier, so the stall counts as exec busy time and in block_ms.

Breakdown over 156 clean boundaries:
- Barrier gap 514 ms: the flush worker's drain write is 413 ms (from 1 Hz flush_worker_checkpoint_seconds deltas), and about 101 ms is exec-thread work (waiting for the layer merge spawned one block earlier, plus merging H-1).
- Serial block 440 ms, of which 147 ms is the serial flush. The candidate's 119 ms is the whole-run mean, which includes tiny pre-bench flushes.
- The serial block without its flush takes 293 ms. A pipelined block with the same fills takes about 318-345 ms.

Costs the fast path keeps or adds:
- A due-checkpoint upkeep at H of about 60 ms: two synchronous layer merges, measured at 24-91 ms on interval checkpoints.
- The serial engine's 25-50 ms speed advantage is lost.
- About 10-20 ms of contention while the flush worker writes. Exec ms per 1k fills is 7% higher during interval writes, upkeep included.

Net saving is about 0.47-0.56 s per epoch per node, out of about 32.4 s. val2 trails the other nodes by 0-4 s at boundaries, so it sets the chain rate; its saving is about 0.47 s.

Two checks rule out hidden offsets:
- Blocks just after a boundary look faster, but that is block content. Fills per block repeat on the epoch cycle: 2k-8k fewer at offsets +7..+20, 3k-8k more at +23..+42. Cost per fill is unchanged.
- Comparing the same height across nodes, a node does not speed up while the other nodes sit in their barriers (+2.2 vs +3.3 ms). So the stalled node's idle time is not used by the others.

At 300m (exec busy 0.995, queue about 60 of 66), saved exec time turns into throughput. Expected: about +1.4% matched/s, which a 600 s n=4 ABBA run (CI about ±0.9%) can resolve.
